# MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1 — Lubrication and fluids - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1
Revision: Rev D (this revision supersedes Rev C)
Plant: P2, line P2-L3
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01

Scope
This document defines lubrication and fluid handling requirements for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) in plant P2, line P2-L3. It covers lubricant selection, supply system checks, fill and drain procedure, contamination control, and record keeping for machining and bearing lubrication points associated with this equipment. This maintenance manual is intended for maintenance technicians, reliability engineers, and shift leaders who perform or supervise fluid servicing tasks. Refer to MM-P2-L3-RR01, SB-1036, and SOP-P2-L3-05 for related electrical lockout requirements, material safety guidance, and mill operating constraints.

Background and rationale
Effective lubrication prevents premature wear, maintains dimensional stability of rings during machining, and reduces the risk of fluid-related contamination in downstream processes. The maximum ring outer diameter for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is 1115 mm. Lubricant selection and handling must protect machine components while remaining compatible with workpiece metallurgical requirements and downstream cleaning processes. The lubricant specified for the machine is supplied under part number CFW-LUB-225; use only this part number for replenishment to ensure chemical compatibility and warranty compliance.

Tools
- Clean fluid transfer pump or dispensing nozzle compatible with CFW-LUB-225 and with nonmetallic seals.
- Approved containers for storage and waste that meet SB-1036 requirements and show the part number CFW-LUB-225 on labels.
- Clean lint‑free rags and particle-free funnels for fluid transfer.
- Inspection mirror and flashlight for visual checks of reservoirs, lines, and seals.
- Sample bottles and labels for fluid analysis; label each sample with machine id EQ-P2-L3-RR01 and location.
- Personal protective equipment per SB-1036 and SOP-P2-L3-05.

Procedure
Preparation
- Confirm that work is authorized per SOP-P2-L3-05 and that electrical and mechanical isolation is in place per facility lockout procedures referenced in MM-P2-L3-RR01.
- Verify that the supply stock matches part number CFW-LUB-225 before opening any containers. Do not mix alternate fluids or unidentified material with system fluid.

Drain and inspection
- Isolate the system and position waste containment to capture all drained fluid. Using clean transfer equipment, drain the reservoirs and primary sumps to waste containers labeled with CFW-LUB-225 as applicable.
- Visually inspect drained fluid for contamination indicators such as particulate, color change, or phase separation. Collect a representative sample in an approved bottle and label it with the equipment id EQ-P2-L3-RR01 and drain location for lab analysis if contamination is suspected.

Cleaning and component check
- Wipe accessible reservoir interiors with lint‑free rags until no visible build up remains. Inspect seals, sight glasses, and filters for damage or excessive wear. Replace damaged items before refilling; consult MM-P2-L3-RR01 for parts identification.
- Check supply lines and fittings for leaks. Tighten fittings to secure-but-not-overstressed condition; if threads or fittings are damaged, replace them per MM-P2-L3-RR01 parts guidance.

Refill
- Filter incoming supply through an approved filter media compatible with CFW-LUB-225 during transfer. Pour or pump fluid into reservoirs gently to minimize aeration. Use labeled funnels and clean hose assemblies exclusively reserved for CFW-LUB-225 to avoid cross-contamination.
- Operate the lubrication system at low speed per SOP-P2-L3-05 until fluid circulates and air pockets are purged. Observe sight glasses and check for external leaks. If foaming or persistent aeration is observed, stop and investigate before resuming.

Post-service verification
- Run the machine through a no-load verification routine per SOP-P2-L3-05 to confirm lubrication flow to bearings and slides. Monitor for abnormal noise or vibration; if present, isolate and investigate.
- Complete system level checks and mark reservoirs with the date of service and the technician's name in the maintenance log.

Examples and special cases
- When machining rings near the maximum allowed outer diameter of 1115 mm special attention must be given to coolant containment and chip separation to limit contaminant ingress into lubrication reservoirs. Modify guards and chip flow paths as necessary to prevent swarf from entering fluid returns.
- If unexpected contamination is found in a collected sample, follow the escalation path in MM-P2-L3-RR01 for analysis and corrective action. Retain samples and records until analysis is complete.

Contamination control and waste handling
- Store CFW-LUB-225 in sealed containers and restrict transfer equipment use to this lubricant only. Label storage with the part number CFW-LUB-225 and equipment id EQ-P2-L3-RR01 where dedicated supply is located.
- Waste fluids and contaminated rags must be handled and disposed of according to SB-1036. Maintain waste manifests and disposal receipts in the maintenance file.

Acceptance criteria
- Reservoirs and lubrication delivery lines must show no visible contamination after servicing and no unplanned leaks during no-load verification run. Bearings and moving interfaces must receive lubricant flow as verified during post-service checks described in SOP-P2-L3-05.
- Only fluid matching part number CFW-LUB-225 may be present in the system after service. Any deviation requires immediate reporting and corrective action as defined in MM-P2-L3-RR01.
- Records must include the technician name, equipment id EQ-P2-L3-RR01, lubricant part number CFW-LUB-225, sample identifiers, and a concise description of any anomalies. Store records in the equipment maintenance file and reference them in future service activities.

Records to keep
- Service log entry referencing this document id MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1 and related document ids MM-P2-L3-RR01, SB-1036, SOP-P2-L3-05.
- Sample labels and laboratory results when contamination is suspected.
- Waste disposal documentation per SB-1036 requirements.
- Inspection checklists and post-service verification notes retained with the EQ-P2-L3-RR01 maintenance file.

References
- MM-P2-L3-RR01
- SB-1036
- SOP-P2-L3-05
